FADE IN:

EXT. PURGATORY - WHITE ROOM - ETERNITY

We see an endless expanse of white, like an infinite waiting room. People are scattered about, some standing, some sitting, others wandering aimlessly. It's been 2 million years since humanity arrived in this desolate realm. The initial hope and determination have given way to madness.

We see MARILYN MONROE, dressed in her iconic "Some Like It Hot" outfit, but her hair is disheveled, and her makeup is smeared. She's standing in front of a blank wall, whispering to herself.

MARILYN MONROE
(to herself)
If I just stand here long enough, the camera will start rolling, and I'll be a star again...

Suddenly, a figure approaches her. It's LEONARDO DA VINCI, looking every bit the Renaissance man. He's wearing a long, white beard and carrying a staff.

LEONARDO DA VINCI
Marilyn, my dear, you've been standing there for eons. It's time to move on.

MARILYN MONROE
(looking at him with vacant eyes)
Who are you? What's your name?

LEONARDO DA VINCI
I am Leonardo da Vinci. I painted the Mona Lisa, designed flying machines...

MARILYN MONROE
(interrupting)
Oh, I know! You're the guy who drew pictures of flying things! Can you draw me a picture of a bird?

Leonardo sighs and begins to draw in the air with his finger. Marilyn watches, mesmerized.

CUT TO:

A group of people huddled together, whispering among themselves. There's CHARLES DARWIN, JESUS CHRIST, and CHARLIE CHAPLIN.

CHARLES DARWIN
...and then I realized, it's not just survival of the fittest. It's survival of the sane.

JESUS CHRIST
(putting his hand on Darwin's shoulder)
Fear not, my friend. We shall be redeemed.

CHARLIE CHAPLIN
(mimicking Jesus)
Redeemed? Ha! We're stuck in this never-ending purgatory!

Suddenly, WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE bursts into the group.

WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE
Hark! What light through yonder madness breaks?

CHARLES DARWIN
Ah, Shakespeare! You've arrived just in time. We're discussing the meaning of life.

WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE
 Meaning of life? Ha! I wrote about that. It's all just a stage, and we're but poor players...

The group nods in agreement, except for Charlie Chaplin, who's now juggling three invisible balls.

CUT TO:

A figure sitting on the floor, surrounded by piles of books. It's ALBERT EINSTEIN, looking like a mad scientist.

ALBERT EINSTEIN
(to himself)
If I just solve this one equation, I'll unlock the secrets of the universe...

Suddenly, MARIE CURIE approaches him.

MARIE CURIE
Albert, dear, you've been working on that equation for eons. Maybe it's time to take a break?

ALBERT EINSTEIN
(looking up)
Marie! I've almost got it! Just a few more calculations...

MARIE CURIE
(sighing)
I'll leave you to your work, then.

She walks away, passing by FRIEDRICH NIETZSCHE, who's standing in front of a blank canvas, staring at it intensely.

FRIEDRICH NIETZSCHE
(to himself)
I will create a masterpiece, one that will shake the very foundations of existence...

As she walks further, she passes by a group of people playing a game of chess. There's BONO, LEO TOLSTOY, and STEPHEN HAWKING.

BONO
(checkmating Tolstoy)
Ha! You should have seen that coming, Leo!

LEO TOLSTOY
(shaking his head)
I've been playing this game for so long, I've lost track of time...

STEPHEN HAWKING
(communicating through his speech-generating device)
I've calculated the odds of winning in this game. It's all just a matter of probability...

CUT TO:

A figure standing on a soapbox, preaching to a crowd of onlookers. It's ELVIS PRESLEY, dressed in his iconic gold lamé suit.

ELVIS PRESLEY
Thank ya, thank ya very much! We're all just waiting for the other shoe to drop, folks! The apocalypse, the rapture, the great beyond...

The crowd applauds, except for one person, who's standing off to the side, looking skeptical. It's RICHARD DAWKINS.

RICHARD DAWKINS
(scoffing)
Apocalypse? Rapture? Don't

FADE IN:

EXT. PURGATORY - 2,000,000 YEARS LATER

The camera pans over an endless, blank white space, devoid of any features or landmarks. The only sound is the distant murmur of whispers and the occasional scream.

We see a group of people huddled together, their faces gaunt and their eyes sunken. They're dressed in tattered and worn-out clothing, a testament to the countless years they've spent in this desolate place.

Suddenly, a figure emerges from the crowd. It's LEONARDO DA VINCI, his famous beard now long and unkempt. He looks around frantically, as if searching for something.

LEONARDO
(to himself)
Two million years... It's been two million years since we arrived. Where is everyone?

He spots a figure sitting on the floor, rocking back and forth. It's ALBERT EINSTEIN, his hair disheveled and his eyes vacant.

LEONARDO
(approaching Einstein)
Albert, my friend! What's wrong?

EINSTEIN
(staring blankly)
I... I forgot. I forgot what I was thinking.

LEONARDO
(gently)
It's okay, Albert. We'll figure it out together.

As Leonardo tries to comfort Einstein, a commotion erupts from the crowd. WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE is standing on a makeshift stage, reciting a monologue from "Hamlet."

SHAKESPEARE
(with wild eyes)
"To be or not to be, that is the question! Whether 'tis nobler to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune..."

The crowd begins to chant along, their voices growing louder and more frenzied.

LEONARDO
(covering his ears)
Stop! Stop this madness!

But it's too late. The chanting becomes a cacophony of screams and wails, as the crowd descends into chaos.

Suddenly, a figure emerges from the shadows. It's MARIE CURIE, her eyes glowing with an otherworldly intensity.

CURIE
(raising her hands)
Enough! We must not give in to madness!

The crowd slowly quiets down, their eyes fixed on Curie.

LEONARDO
(approaching Curie)
Marie, what's happening to us?

CURIE
( gravely)
We've been here for too long. Our minds are deteriorating. We must find a way to keep ourselves sane.

As Curie speaks, we see flashes of other historical figures, each struggling to maintain their grip on reality:

* CHARLES DARWIN, scribbling notes on a makeshift chalkboard, trying to remember his theory of evolution.
* GALILEO GALILEI, staring at the blank ceiling, searching for the stars he once studied.
* FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE, tending to a makeshift hospital, caring for the sick and injured.
* CHARLIE CHAPLIN, performing a silent comedy routine, trying to bring laughter to the desolate space.
* MICHAELANGELO, sculpting a figure from a block of imaginary marble, his hands moving deftly in the air.
* VINCENT VAN GOGH, painting vivid masterpieces on the blank walls, his colors bursting with life.
* ELVIS PRESLEY, strumming an invisible guitar, singing "Can't Help Falling in Love."
* FREDERICK NIKOLAI, attempting to solve a complex mathematical equation, his brow furrowed in concentration.
* ANDREW JACKSON, leading a group of people in a rousing chorus of "The Battle Hymn of the Republic."
* FRIDA KAHLO, her face a mask of pain, as she paints a self-portrait on her own face.
* ALBERT CAMUS, writing in a journal, his words pouring out in a stream of consciousness.
* GEORGIA O'KEEFE, arranging a bouquet of imaginary flowers, her eyes closed in ecstasy.
* PABLO PICASSO, creating a cubist masterpiece on the floor, his hands moving with frenetic energy.
* VIRGINIA WOOLF, scribbling in a journal, her words flowing like a river.
* MARTIN LUTHER KING JR., standing on a soapbox, delivering a passionate speech, his voice ringing out across the void.
* RENÉ DESCARTES, pacing back and forth, muttering "I think, therefore I am."
* JANE AUSTEN, writing a novel on a imaginary typewriter, her words flowing like a stream.
* NIKOLA TESLA, tinkering with a makeshift invention, his eyes shining with excitement.
* LEONARDO BRUNI, studying a book on philosophy, his brow furrowed in concentration.
* Sigmund FREUD, analyzing a patient on a makeshift couch, his eyes piercing.
* Cleopatra, standing on a throne, ruling over the chaos with an iron fist.

FADE IN:

EXT. PURGATORY - INFINITE WAITING ROOM - 2 MILLION YEARS LATER

The camera pans across an endless, featureless white expanse. The only sound is the soft hum of fluorescent lights overhead. People sit, stand, or pace, their faces etched with desperation and madness. 90% of humanity has lost its grip on sanity after eons in this limbo.

We see:

* Leonardo da Vinci frantically scribbling equations on the wall with a piece of chalk, muttering to himself about flying machines.
* Marie Curie, her eyes sunken, clutching a vial of glowing substance, whispering "Radioactivity...the answer is in radioactivity..."
* Napoleon Bonaparte, pacing back and forth, shouting orders to an invisible army.
* William Shakespeare, scribbling in a tattered notebook, muttering "To be or not to be...to be or not to be..."
* Albert Einstein, staring at a chalkboard filled with complex equations, his hair wild and unkempt.
* Cleopatra, lounging on a nearby couch, applying makeup to her face, cooing "I am the queen...I am the queen..."
* Vincent van Gogh, painting vivid masterpieces on the wall with his fingers, tears streaming down his face.
* Martin Luther King Jr., preaching to a crowd of vacant-eyed onlookers, his voice hoarse from years of shouting.
* Galileo Galilei, staring up at the ceiling, whispering "The earth revolves around the sun...the earth revolves around the sun..."
* Frida Kahlo, her face a mess of scars, creating vibrant artwork on the walls with her own blood.
* Charles Darwin, scribbling in a notebook, muttering "Survival of the fittest...but what am I surviving for?"
* Sigmund Freud, analyzing the actions of those around him, nodding thoughtfully to himself.
* Jane Austen, writing novels on scraps of paper, her quill pen scratching out words.
* Alexander the Great, pacing back and forth, planning conquests that will never come.
* Mahatma Gandhi, meditating peacefully, a look of serene calm on his face.
* Charles Dickens, writing in a leather-bound book, his eyes twinkling with creativity.
* Florence Nightingale, tending to the imaginary wounds of those around her, cooing softly.
* Rembrandt van Rijn, painting masterpieces on the walls, his eyes gleaming with inspiration.
* Ada Lovelace, scribbling code on scraps of paper, her mind racing with mathematical concepts.
* Benjamin Franklin, flying a kite made of scraps of fabric and wire, laughing maniacally.
* Emily Dickinson, scribbling poetry on the walls, her eyes closed in rapture.
* Johannes Gutenberg, printing out books on a makeshift press, his hands moving with a life of their own.
* Michelangelo, sculpting masterpieces from the walls themselves, his chisel striking true.
* Elizabeth I, holding court, her regal demeanor unwavering despite the madness around her.
* Genghis Khan, riding an invisible horse, shouting orders to his non-existent army.
* Stephen Hawking, scribbling equations on a blackboard, his eyes shining with intensity.
* Martin Luther, nailing theses to the wall, his face set in determination.
* Beethoven, composing symphonies on an invisible piano, his eyes closed in ecstasy.
* Catherine the Great, ruling over her kingdom of vacant-eyed subjects, her voice firm and commanding.
* Abraham Lincoln, delivering the Gettysburg Address to an audience of catatonic onlookers, his voice ringing out across the void.

As the camera pans out, we see that the remaining 10% of humanity huddles together in a corner, clinging to each other in a desperate bid for sanity.

* The group is led by a frail but determined-looking Isaac Newton, who whispers words of comfort to the others.
* Nearby, a calm and collected Amelia Earhart plots a course to nowhere on a makeshift map.
* A young and energetic Steve Jobs tinkers with a nonexistent iPhone, his eyes shining with innovation.
* A serene and peaceful Dalai Lama mediates, his eyes closed in contemplation.

As the camera continues to pan out, we see the infinite expanse of the waiting room, stretching out in every direction. The sound of madness and despair grows fainter, replaced by the soft hum of fluorescent lights and the distant whispers of the sane.

FADE TO BLACK.

Note: The screenplay does not end here, the story could continue, there are many directions the story could go from here.

FADE IN:

EXT. PURGATORY WAITING ROOM - DAY

We see an endless, white, blank space stretching out before us. The camera pans across the room, revealing millions of people, all standing still, expressionless, and silent. It's as if time has stood still.

CUT TO:

A group of people huddled in the corner, muttering to themselves. We see Napoleon Bonaparte, wearing his iconic bicorne hat, rocking back and forth, repeating the phrase "I should have won at Waterloo" over and over. Next to him is Vincent van Gogh, painting an endless canvas of swirling colors with his eyes closed. Frida Kahlo sits nearby, her face a mesh of bandages, humming a soft tune.

Suddenly, Albert Einstein bursts into the group, his wild hair sticking out in every direction. "Eureka!" he exclaims. "I've finally solved the equation of purgatory!" He scribbles furiously on a chalkboard that appears out of thin air.

Leonardo da Vinci looks up from his sketchbook, raises an eyebrow, and says, "Ah, Albie, my friend, you've been saying that for 1.9 million years. I think it's time to take a break." Einstein ignores him and continues scribbling.

William Shakespeare strolls by, reciting lines from Hamlet. "To be or not to be, that is the question...whether 'tis nobler in the mind to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune..." He stops in front of Cleopatra, who is practicing her royal wave in front of a mirror that isn't there. "Good morrow, fair queen," he says with a bow.

Cleopatra curtsies, then turns back to her mirror, admiring her reflection. Nearby, Marie Antoinette is having a tea party with a group of invisible friends. "Let them eat cake!" she cackles maniacally.

CUT TO:

A group of philosophers engaged in a heated debate. Plato argues with Socrates, while Aristotle looks on, shaking his head. Immanuel Kant sits in the corner, writing in a journal, muttering about the categorical imperative. Friedrich Nietzsche paces back and forth, ranting about the will to power.

Suddenly, Alexander the Great bursts into the group, sword in hand. "I will conquer this purgatory!" he shouts. "I will not rest until I have claimed this place as my own!" The philosophers stare at him, unimpressed.

CUT TO:

A group of artists gathered around a blank canvas. Pablo Picasso is painting a Cubist masterpiece, while Claude Monet is creating a water lily landscape. Johannes Vermeer is adjusting the light on a still life, while Rembrandt is etching a self-portrait. Salvador Dali is melting clocks in the corner, laughing maniacally.

CUT TO:

A group of musicians playing a cacophonous symphony. Ludwig van Beethoven pounds away at a piano, while Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart conducts an invisible orchestra. Jimi Hendrix plays a psychedelic guitar solo, while John Lennon strums a gentle melody on an acoustic guitar. Elvis Presley dances the twist, shaking his hips to an unheard beat.

CUT TO:

A group of writers typing away on invisible typewriters. Ernest Hemingway is writing a sparse, minimalist novel, while Jane Austen is crafting a witty romance. Charles Dickens is scribbling a sprawling epic, while Edgar Allan Poe is penning a dark poem. Virginia Woolf is writing a stream-of-consciousness novel, while Mark Twain is spinning a yarn about Tom Sawyer.

CUT TO:

A group of scientists conducting experiments. Galileo Galilei is measuring the distance to the ceiling, while Isaac Newton is calculating the trajectory of an invisible apple. Charles Darwin is studying the evolution of the waiting room's furniture, while Marie Curie is discovering the secrets of the room's eerie glow.

CUT TO:

A group of leaders holding a meeting. Abraham Lincoln is delivering a speech, while Mahatma Gandhi is leading a silent protest. Nelson Mandela is negotiating a peace treaty, while Martin Luther King Jr. is dreaming of a better tomorrow.

Suddenly, a figure appears at the edge of the room. It's the ghost of Jesus Christ, carrying a sign that reads "Repent Now". The room falls silent as the figure begins to speak.

"The wait is almost over," it says. "Your time in purgatory is drawing to a close. Prepare yourselves for the next stage of your journey."

The room erupts into chaos as the inhabitants of purgatory react to the news. Some rejoice, others despair. The camera zooms out, showing the endless expanse of the waiting room, as the words "To Be Continued..." appear on the screen.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.

Other notable figures in the waiting room include:

* Buddha, meditating in the corner.
